groups.title: Tablet (C31700ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness, during growth and in old age; for the relief of dryness of the eyes; for night blindness; for the prevention of poor development of bones and teeth and of rickets; for the prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anaemia; and for the supply of zinc.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A a day may cause birth defects. Women who are within the first 3 months of pregnancy or who may be pregnant must not take it. An overdose in a child aged 6 years or younger can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep this medicine out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have hypercalcaemia (an excess of calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease, high blood potassium, Wilson's disease, haemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas because of abnormal iron metabolism), haemosiderosis, anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency, kidney stones or severe renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the child gets a lot of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have hyperoxaluria (a state in which an excessive amount of oxalate is excreted in the urine); if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have gallbladder disease, liver disease, acute or chronic bronchitis, pulmonary oedema, alkalosis, peptic ulcer or gout; if you have or have had kidney stones; if you have a tendency to thrombosis; or if you are short of folic acid.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. It may interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with cardiac glycosides, an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful swelling of the joints, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, loose stools, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, skin rash, urticaria, itching, photosensitivity reactions, abdominal or stomach pain, cramps, fever, coma, upper abdominal pain, allergic reactions, angioedema, joint pain, eosinophilia, iodine poisoning, high blood potassium, wind, stomach pain, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, low blood pressure, pulmonary oedema, or menstruation that comes earlier than expected, gradually increases in amount or lasts a long time.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6, C and of zinc, relief of dry eyes and night blindness, prevention of poor bone and tooth development and rickets, and prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anaemia

groups.title: Soft Capsule (A06300ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for obesity and for the improvement of lipid metabolism in diabetic and essential hypercholesterolaemia.
groups.usage: Take 3 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes before meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to soybean oil, soybean or peanut.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; if a particular risk is expected from fat overload; if you have a tendency to thrombosis; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Consult a pharmacist before using it together with levodopa, an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen or an intravenous lipid preparation.

If menstruation comes earlier than expected, gradually increases in amount or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash and reddening of the skin may occur.

groups.title: Enteric-Coated Tablet (117801ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acute and chronic constipation, before and after surgery, for clearing faeces from the bowel, and for clearing faeces from the bowel for X-ray examination.
groups.usage: Adults: take 2 tablets (10 mg), 1 time in 1 day, at bedtime. Depending on symptoms, the amount per dose may be increased to 3 tablets (15 mg).
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis, acute enteritis and the like), intestinal paralysis, intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), spastic constipation, severely hardened stools, an anal fissure (a tear), severe dehydration, abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child, if you are an older person, or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4.

Do not chew it when taking it. Do not use it continuously for more than 1 week.

Do not take it together with a diuretic, an adrenocortical hormone preparation, a medicine that causes polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, or an antacid. Do not take this medicine within 1 hour after drinking milk.

If angioedema, signs of anaphylaxis, abdominal discomfort such as cramps or stomach ache, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, an urge to pass urine, headache, back pain, dizziness or fainting occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E94800ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Ages 8 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Take it 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking this medicine and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have ever had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure; or if you have severe acute or chronic kidney disease or renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have had sudden abdominal pain in connection with pseudoephedrine; if you have an allergic constitution; if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, glaucoma or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you have lost fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea or cannot take in fluid; if you are taking a diuretic; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Do not take it continuously for a long period. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines). Consult a pharmacist if you have been given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, stomach discomfort, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia; rarely shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters); asthma; posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance); or Conn's syndrome of unknown frequency.

Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol or flucloxacillin. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash, reddening of the skin, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, high anion gap metabolic acidosis; rarely signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters over the whole skin or on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes); asthma; general lassitude; jaundice; interstitial pneumonia (cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever); or symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance).

groups.title: Cream (131303CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for disinfecting wounded areas of skin over a small area.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area several times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have had hypersensitivity to it, and do not use it on mucous membranes such as the vagina, bladder or mouth, or in the eye.

Consult a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to other medicines, if you have or have had an allergic disease such as asthma or a family history of it, or if you may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Use this medicine externally only.

Contact with the eye may cause serious corneal damage that can require a corneal transplant (corneal erosion, epithelial defect or corneal damage, serious permanent visual impairment), so take care to keep it out of the eyes; if it does get into the eye, wash it out immediately and thoroughly with clean water.

Organic material such as serum or pus, and soaps, weaken the disinfectant action of this medicine, so wash them off thoroughly before use.

If, rarely, shock (for example nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, chest tightness, difficulty breathing, reddening of the skin) or, occasionally, hypersensitivity such as rash or urticaria occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Fatal anaphylactic shock and photosensitisation of unknown frequency may occur.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fungal skin infections: tinea (tinea corporis, tinea cruris, tinea pedis), cutaneous candidiasis, tinea versicolor and seborrhoeic dermatitis.

Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, or on a scalp that is wounded or inflamed, or on severely eroded areas.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, if the user is a child, or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to propylene glycol.

In candidiasis, do not use an acidic soap. Do not use an occlusive dressing or wrapping unless a doctor tells you to. Use this medicine externally only. Do not use it in the eye; apply it carefully so that it does not touch the eye, and if it accidentally gets into the eye, wash it out completely with plenty of water.

Consult a pharmacist before using it together with an antifungal of the same class (miconazole, econazole, isoconazole and the like).

At the site of application, contact dermatitis, rash, a hot feeling of the skin, peeling of the skin, blistering rash, sticky skin, hypersensitivity, erythema, itching, dryness, irritation, bleeding, discomfort, inflammation, abnormal sensation and, very rarely, urticaria, pain and burns may occur.
